title: Lovers
text:
a flower

not far from night

my mute body

opens

to the delicate urgency of dew
editorial_note: The body, flower, and night are left in apposition without explanatory links; dew retains its paradoxical delicacy and urgency.

title: Tiny Lady…
text:
Tiny lady

dwelling in the heart of a bird

goes out at dawn to utter one syllable

NO
editorial_note: The diminutive figure’s entire dawn utterance remains the capitalized refusal; moradora is rendered as dwelling to keep her inhabitation active.

title: This Lilac Sheds Its Petals…
text:
This lilac sheds its petals.

Out of itself it falls

and hides its ancient shadow.

I shall die of things like this.
editorial_note: Desde sí misma becomes out of itself, preserving the flower’s self-originating fall and the speaker’s fatal susceptibility to such small transformations.

text:
Strange, to unaccustom myself

to the hour in which I was born.

Strange, no longer to ply

the trade of the newly arrived.
editorial_note: Extraño is held as the adjective strange rather than resolved into I miss; birth persists as an hour and newcomer as a lifelong profession.

title: Communications
text:
The wind had eaten away

part of my face and my hands.

They called me ragged angel.

I waited.
editorial_note: The title’s promise of exchange contracts into mutilation, a name imposed by others, and the unresolved final act of waiting.

title: The Lack
text:
I know nothing of birds,

I do not know the history of fire.

But I believe my solitude ought to have wings.
editorial_note: The repeated not-knowing remains plain; wings emerge not as knowledge or escape but as something solitude ought ethically or imaginatively to possess.

title: Strange That I Was…
text:
strange that I was

when, neighbor to distant lights,

I treasured words of utter purity

to create new silences
editorial_note: The paradox of being neighbor to distant lights is retained, as is the transformation of pure words into newly made silences.

title: Ballad of the Weeping Stone
text:
death dies laughing but life

dies weeping but death but life

but nothing nothing nothing
editorial_note: The lowercase rush and repeated pero remain unpunctuated; death and life cancel each other until only the triple nothing is left.
